nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $m$ be coprime natural numbers with $0 < n < m$. Since $\gcd(m - n, nm) = 1$, the residue of $m - n$ is invertible in $\mathbb{Z}/nm\mathbb{Z}$; write $u$ for its inverse. Then the equalities $a^{m-1} = (a^{m-n} - 1)\,u\,n + a^{m-n}$ and $(a^{m-n} - 1)\,u\,n + a^{m-n} = (a^{m-n} - 1)\,u\,m + 1$ in $\mathbb{Z}/nm\mathbb{Z}$ hold for every integer $a$ coprime to $nm$ if and only if both $n$ and $m$ have…
nodes.title: Fermat's congruence for a product of coprime moduli

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime. Then $p$ is a Sophie Germain prime if and only if $a^{2p} \equiv (2p + 1)\,a^{p+1} - 2p \pmod{p(2p + 1)}$ for every integer $a$ coprime to $p(2p + 1)$; and $p$ is a Sophie Germain prime if and only if $(2p + 1)\,a^{p-1} \equiv p\,a^{2p} + p + 1 \pmod{p(2p + 1)}$ for every integer $a$ coprime to $p(2p + 1)$.
nodes.title: Fermat-type characterizations of Sophie Germain primes

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every odd prime $p$, the number $2^n p + 1$ is not a Carmichael number.
nodes.title: Alahmadi–Luca theorem on Carmichael numbers

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $j$ be natural numbers and put $q_{i+1} = 2^i (p + 1) - 1$ for $i \ge 0$, so that $q_1 = p$ and $q_{i+2} = 2q_{i+1} + 1$. Suppose $q_1, \dots, q_{j+2}$ are all prime, and write $q = q_{j+1}$ and $q' = q_{j+2} = 2q + 1$. Then for every integer $a$ coprime to $qq'$, $a^{q'-1} \equiv q'\,a^{q+1} - 2q \pmod{qq'}$ and $q'\,a^{q-1} \equiv q\,a^{q'-1} + q + 1 \pmod{qq'}$.
nodes.title: Fermat-type congruences along a Sophie Germain prime chain

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $\mathrm{ord}_p(2)$ be the multiplicative order of $2$ modulo $p$. Then there is some $j \le \mathrm{ord}_p(2)$ such that $2^j (p + 1) - 1$ is not prime. Thus the Sophie Germain prime chain $q_1 = p$, $q_{i+1} = 2q_i + 1 = 2^i (p + 1) - 1$ begins with at most $\mathrm{ord}_p(2)$ consecutive primes.
nodes.title: Length of a Sophie Germain prime chain

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ be odd, and suppose neither $n$ nor $n + 2$ is a Carmichael number. Then $n$ and $n + 2$ are both prime if and only if $2a^{n+1} \equiv (n + 2)\,a^2 - n \pmod{n(n + 2)}$ for every integer $a$ coprime to $n(n + 2)$; and $n$ and $n + 2$ are both prime if and only if $n\,a^{n+1} \equiv (n + 2)\,a^{n-1} - 2 \pmod{n(n + 2)}$ for every integer $a$ coprime to $n(n + 2)$.
